open_points.subject: FlowEdge endpoint sentinel and flow-version creation
open_points.text: “composition refuses one that does” conflicts with “the version is kept either way” in the compose-and-prove action
open_points.question: When a composition contains a node whose node_id is the empty string, is a FlowVersion created and retained as unproven, or is the composition rejected without creating the version (and, for a new flow_id, without creating the Flow)?
options: Reject without creating a FlowVersion or Flow
Create and retain an unproven FlowVersion, creating the Flow when needed
open_points.default_guess: Reject without creating a FlowVersion or Flow

open_points.subject: FlowEdge unavailable-input condition
open_points.text: “A node one of whose input ports has every incoming edge disabled by its guard, or coming from a skipped node”
open_points.question: For one input port with several incoming edges, exactly which condition causes the node to be skipped: every edge being unavailable for either reason, every edge being guard-disabled, or the presence of any edge from a skipped node?
options: Skip only when every incoming edge is unavailable, each either guard-disabled or sourced from a skipped node
Skip only when every incoming edge is guard-disabled, or when any incoming edge is sourced from a skipped node
Skip whenever any incoming edge is guard-disabled or sourced from a skipped node
open_points.default_guess: Skip only when every incoming edge is unavailable, each either guard-disabled or sourced from a skipped node

open_points.subject: Meaning of skipped source node
open_points.text: “coming from a skipped node” and “is recorded skipped_by_guard” conflict with M23’s distinction between a node not executed because “its guards disabled it” and one recorded upstream_failed because “an upstream node failed”
open_points.question: Does “skipped node” mean only a source recorded skipped_by_guard, or also a source recorded upstream_failed; and what status must propagate when the unavailable source is upstream_failed?
options: Only skipped_by_guard sources trigger this rule; upstream_failed ancestry produces upstream_failed
Both skipped_by_guard and upstream_failed sources trigger this rule and the dependent is always skipped_by_guard
Both source statuses count, but the dependent preserves the causal status
open_points.default_guess: Only skipped_by_guard sources trigger this rule; upstream_failed ancestry produces upstream_failed

open_points.subject: Input ports supplied by constants
open_points.text: “one of whose input ports has every incoming edge disabled” is silent about an input port supplied by a FlowConstant, which may have no incoming edges
open_points.question: Does a constant count as an available delivery when deciding whether an input port causes skipped_by_guard, or does the rule examine edges alone and therefore risk treating a constant-only port’s empty edge set as entirely disabled?
options: A valid constant delivery makes the port available and prevents this skip condition
Only incoming edges participate, so a constant-only port satisfies the no-deliverable-edge condition
The proof forbids constants on ports to which this runtime rule could apply
open_points.default_guess: A valid constant delivery makes the port available and prevents this skip condition

open_points.subject: Mapped-node skip granularity
open_points.text: “A node one of whose input ports … is not executed and is recorded skipped_by_guard” does not say how this applies to a mapped node whose executions and records are distinguished by map_index
open_points.question: When the unavailable-input condition affects only some elements of a mapped node, is skipped_by_guard recorded per map element while other elements execute, or is the entire mapped node skipped?
options: Decide and record skipping independently for each map_index
Skip every execution of the mapped node if any element meets the condition
The condition can only be evaluated for the mapped input as a whole
open_points.default_guess: Decide and record skipping independently for each map_index
